title: Transforming Teacher Education in Developing Countries: The Role of Generative AI in Bridging Theory and Practice
extended_summary:
This perspective paper addresses a structural problem in teacher education in developing countries: programs often emphasize content delivery and standardized assessment while neglecting pedagogical modeling and performance-based assessment. Using Ghana as the main case, the paper argues that these long-standing issues contribute to a gap between theory and classroom practice in initial teacher education, with downstream effects on the readiness of pre-service teachers and eventually K-12 learning outcomes.

The paper does not report an empirical intervention. Instead, it uses a logical deduction approach and reviews recent literature on generative AI (GenAI) in teacher education to argue that tools such as ChatGPT could reduce the time teacher educators spend on content transmission. This, in turn, would allow more attention to pedagogical modeling, authentic assessment, professional development, resource generation, digital literacy, and critical thinking. The paper also notes that GenAI may help teacher educators and pre-service teachers access resources and support lesson planning and other teaching tasks.

The context is Ghanaian initial teacher education, especially four-year college-based programs preparing pre-service teachers for future K-12 classrooms. The paper concludes that GenAI could catalyze broader reform in teacher education if implemented in a scaffolded and responsible way. It warns, however, that misuse of GenAI may undermine critical thinking and creativity, and it recommends GenAI literacy, ethical training, prompt engineering skills, and critical evaluation of AI-generated content.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative artificial intelligence / large language model tools used for content support, drafting, and interactive assistance.
identified_tools.use_case: A perspective/theoretical paper arguing that GenAI could support content knowledge acquisition, pedagogical modeling, performance-based assessment, resource acquisition, digital literacy, critical thinking, and teacher professional development in teacher education.

findings.finding_summary: The paper argues that GenAI could reduce the burden of content delivery in teacher education, freeing time for pedagogical modeling and performance-based assessment, and potentially improving future K-12 learning outcomes. It is presented as a theoretical claim rather than an empirically tested effect; no sample size or effect size is reported.
findings.measure: Theoretical argument about teacher education functions and downstream K-12 learning outcomes

findings.finding_summary: The paper cautions that misuse of GenAI could undermine critical thinking and creativity skills that are currently nurtured through traditional lecture-based teaching and content-based assessments. This is a stated risk in a perspective paper, not an empirically measured outcome.
findings.measure: Potential undermining of critical thinking and creativity

quality_tier_rationale: This is a perspective/theoretical paper with no empirical evaluation, no study sample, and no measured outcomes. The claims are inferential and supported by cited literature rather than original data.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper argues for potentially broad system-level benefits, but these are speculative rather than observed effects. Because no effect sizes or outcome data are reported, impact cannot be quantified and remains unclear.
